key_insight: Cubic HUBO captures substantial third-order configurational energy contributions in lithium-rich oxyfluorides that quadratic QUBO models cannot represent.
engineering_relevance: Higher-order energy models could improve computational screening of disordered-rocksalt cathodes, provided magnetic-state dependence is accounted for.
method: Compute composition-preserving, fixed-geometry energy maps using spin-polarized DFT for LMOF and LMTiOF.
Compare quadratic QUBO and cubic HUBO fits and verify third-order nonadditivity through direct DFT energy differences.
Compare magnetic initializations to assess dependence on the converged electronic state.
evidence_signal: Cubic HUBO substantially reduces fitting errors in both materials, while LMTiOF shows strong electronic-state dependence of its third-order contribution.
watch_item: The fitted higher-order terms are effective couplings among composition-preserving exchange variables, not uniquely identified microscopic three-atom interactions.
paper_title: First-Principles Identification of Higher-Order Configurational Energy Terms and Their Magnetic-State Dependence in Lithium-Rich Oxyfluorides: From QUBO to HUBO
